title_en: Regulations on Radio Administration of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated for the purpose of strengthening radio administration, maintaining the order of airwaves, effectively developing and utilizing radio spectrum resources, and ensuring the normal operation of various radio services.

Article 2 The use of radio frequencies, the establishment and operation of radio stations (including stations), the research, development, production, import, sale, and maintenance of radio transmitting equipment, and the use of non-radio equipment that radiates radio waves within the territory of the People's Republic of China shall comply with these Regulations.
Article 3 Radio spectrum resources belong to the State. The State implements the principles of unified planning, rational development, and compensated use for radio spectrum resources.

Article 4 Radio administration work shall be under the unified leadership of the State Council and the Central Military Commission, with division of labor and levels of responsibility, and shall implement the policy of scientific management, resource protection, safety assurance, and development promotion.

Article 5 The State encourages and supports scientific and technological research on radio spectrum resources and the promotion and application of advanced technologies to improve the utilization efficiency of radio spectrum resources.

Article 6 No unit or individual may use radio frequencies without authorization, cause harmful interference to radio services conducted according to law, or use radio stations (including stations) to engage in illegal or criminal activities.
Article 7 The State may implement radio control when necessary for safeguarding national security, ensuring major national tasks, or handling major emergencies.

Article 8 The national radio regulatory authority shall be responsible for radio administration nationwide, formulate guidelines and policies for radio administration in accordance with its functions, uniformly manage radio frequencies and radio stations (including stations), be responsible for radio monitoring, interference investigation, and foreign-related radio administration, and coordinate and handle matters related to radio administration.

Article 9 The electromagnetic spectrum regulatory authority of the Chinese People's Liberation Army shall be responsible for radio administration within the military system and participate in the formulation of national guidelines and policies concerning radio administration.

Article 10 The radio regulatory authorities of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, under the leadership of the national radio regulatory authority and the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, shall be responsible for radio administration within their respective administrative regions, excluding the military system, implement radio frequency use licenses in accordance with their approval authority, examine the construction layout and site selection of radio stations (including stations), issue radio station licenses and radio station identification codes (including call signs, hereinafter the same), be responsible for radio monitoring and interference investigation within their administrative regions, and coordinate and handle matters related to radio administration within their administrative regions.
The radio regulatory authorities of provinces and autonomous regions may, as necessary for the work, establish dispatched agencies within their administrative regions. The dispatched agencies shall perform their functions within the scope of authorization granted by the radio regulatory authorities of provinces and autonomous regions.

Article 11 The military and local authorities shall establish a coordination mechanism for radio administration, jointly demarcate radio frequencies, and consult and handle matters concerning radio administration between the military system and non-military systems. Major issues concerning radio administration shall be reported to the State Council and the Central Military Commission for decision.

Article 12 The radio regulatory authorities of the relevant departments of the State Council shall, under the professional guidance of the national radio regulatory authority, be responsible for radio administration within their respective systems (industries), implement and enforce the national guidelines, policies, laws, administrative regulations, and rules on radio administration, manage the aeronautical and maritime radio dedicated frequencies allocated by the national radio regulatory authority for use by their systems (industries) in accordance with these Regulations and the departmental functions prescribed by the State Council, plan the construction layout and site selection of radio stations (including stations) within their systems (industries), and issue standard radio station licenses and radio station identification codes.

Article 13 The national radio regulatory authority shall be responsible for formulating regulations on radio frequency allocation and making them public.
When formulating regulations on radio frequency allocation, the opinions of the relevant departments of the State Council and relevant military units shall be solicited, and full consideration shall be given to the needs of national security, economic and social development, scientific and technological progress, and effective utilization of spectrum resources.

Article 16 The radio regulatory authority shall complete the review within 20 working days from the date of accepting the application for a radio frequency use license, and shall, in accordance with the conditions specified in Article 15 of these Regulations and taking into full consideration the needs of national security and the availability of frequencies, make a decision to grant or deny the license. If the license is granted, a radio frequency use license certificate shall be issued; if the license is denied, a written notice shall be given to the applicant with reasons.
The radio frequency use license certificate shall specify the purpose, scope of use, usage rate requirements, term of use, and other matters of the radio frequency.

Article 17 The licensing of commercial radio frequencies such as those used for terrestrial public mobile communications may be conducted by means of bidding or auction in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations.
After determining the successful bidder or buyer through bidding or auction, the radio regulatory authority shall make a decision to grant the license and, according to law, issue a radio frequency use license certificate to the successful bidder or buyer.

Article 18 Radio frequency use licenses shall be granted by the national radio regulatory authority. Radio frequency use licenses within the scope determined by the national radio regulatory authority shall be granted by the radio regulatory authorities of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government.
The maritime radio dedicated frequencies allocated by the national radio regulatory authority for use by the transportation, fishery, and marine systems (industries) shall be licensed by the radio regulatory authorities of the provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government where they are located, in conjunction with the relevant competent departments; the aeronautical radio dedicated frequencies allocated by the national radio regulatory authority for use by the civil aviation system shall be licensed by the competent civil aviation authority under the State Council.

Article 19 The term of a radio frequency use license shall not exceed 10 years.
Where continued use is required after the expiration of the term of a radio frequency use license, an application for renewal shall be submitted to the radio regulatory authority that made the licensing decision at least 30 working days before the expiration of the term. The radio regulatory authority accepting the application shall review and make a decision in accordance with the provisions of Articles 15 and 16 of these Regulations.
Where a party intends to terminate the use of a radio frequency before the expiration of the term of the radio frequency use license, it shall timely go through the cancellation procedures with the radio regulatory authority that made the licensing decision.

Article 20 Where the right to use a radio frequency is to be transferred, the transferee shall meet the conditions specified in Article 15 of these Regulations and submit a transfer agreement between the parties, and shall apply to the radio regulatory authority for approval in accordance with the procedures specified in Article 16 of these Regulations.

Article 21 The use of radio frequencies shall be subject to the payment of radio frequency occupation fees in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.
The items and standards of radio frequency occupation fees shall be formulated by the financial department and the competent department of pricing of the State Council.

Article 22 Satellite radio frequencies allocated to China by the International Telecommunication Union in accordance with international rules shall be uniformly assigned by the national radio regulatory authority to the user units.
An application for the use of satellite radio frequencies not planned by the International Telecommunication Union shall be submitted uniformly through the national radio regulatory authority. The national radio regulatory authority shall promptly organize the relevant units to carry out necessary domestic coordination, and undertake international notification, coordination and registration in accordance with international rules.

Article 23 Where the establishment of a satellite communication network requires the use of satellite radio frequencies, in addition to meeting the conditions set forth in Article 15 of these Regulations, the applicant shall also provide information such as the intended space radio station, satellite orbital position and satellite coverage area, as well as supporting materials evidencing the completion of domestic coordination and the conduct of necessary international coordination.

Article 24 Where a person uses satellite radio frequencies of other countries or regions to conduct business, he/she shall comply with the provisions on the management of satellite radio frequencies of China, and complete coordination with the satellite radio frequencies declared by China.

Article 25 For the construction of a satellite project, a feasibility demonstration of the intended satellite radio frequencies shall be conducted at the project planning stage; for the construction of a satellite project that requires approval from the State Council and the Central Military Commission, the intended satellite radio frequencies shall be negotiated and determined with the national radio regulatory authority at the project planning stage.

Article 26 Unless caused by force majeure, where a person, after obtaining a radio frequency use permit, fails to use the frequency for more than 2 years or the utilization rate fails to meet the requirements stipulated in the license, the radio regulatory authority that made the licensing decision shall have the right to revoke the radio frequency use permit and reclaim the radio frequency.

Article 29 An applicant for establishing and using an amateur radio station shall be familiar with radio management provisions, possess corresponding operational technical capabilities, and the radio transmitting equipment used shall comply with national standards and the relevant provisions on national radio management.

Article 30 The establishment and use of a radio station (or station) with a fixed site shall be subject to the licensing by the radio regulatory authority of the province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government where the radio station (or station) is located. The establishment and use of a radio station without a fixed site shall be subject to the licensing by the radio regulatory authority of the province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government where the applicant's domicile is located.
The establishment and use of space radio stations, satellite telemetry, tracking and command (navigation) stations, satellite gateway stations, international private leased circuit earth stations, short-wave radio stations (or stations) of 15 watts or more, and other important radio stations (or stations) involving national sovereignty or security shall be subject to the licensing by the national radio regulatory authority.

Article 31 The radio regulatory authority shall complete the review within 30 working days from the date of accepting the application, and make a decision on granting or denying the license in accordance with the conditions prescribed in Articles 28 and 29 of these Regulations. If the license is granted, a radio station license shall be issued, and if a radio station identification code is required, the radio station identification code shall be issued concurrently; if the license is denied, the applicant shall be notified in writing with reasons given.
Where a radio station (or station) needs to modify or add a radio station identification code, the radio regulatory authority shall issue it.

Article 32 A radio station license shall specify the site of the radio station (or station), frequency used, transmission power, validity period, usage requirements and other matters.
The format of the radio station license shall be uniformly prescribed by the national radio regulatory authority.

Article 33 Where the radio frequency used by a radio station (or station) is subject to a radio frequency use permit, the validity period of its radio station license shall not exceed the period specified in the radio frequency use permit; where the radio frequency use permit is not required pursuant to Article 14 of these Regulations, the validity period of its radio station license shall not exceed 5 years.
Where it is necessary to continue using the radio station (or station) after the expiration of the validity period of the radio station license, an application for replacing the radio station license shall be submitted to the radio regulatory authority that made the licensing decision no later than 30 working days before the expiration of the period. The radio regulatory authority that accepts the application shall make a decision in accordance with Article 31 of these Regulations.

Article 34 The national radio regulatory authority shall uniformly apply to the International Telecommunication Union for radio station identification code sequences, and shall compile and allocate radio station identification codes.

Article 35 The site selection for the construction of a radio station (or station) with a fixed site shall comply with the requirements of urban and rural planning, and avoid buildings, facilities and the like that may affect its function. Where a local people's government formulates or modifies urban and rural planning, and arranges construction projects that may affect the function of a large radio station (or station), it shall take into account the needs for the function of the radio station, and solicit opinions from the local radio regulatory authority and the military electromagnetic spectrum management authority.
For the establishment of large radio stations (or stations) and terrestrial public mobile communication base stations, the layout plan of their sites shall meet the requirements of resource sharing and electromagnetic environmental protection.

Article 36 The establishment and use of standard-type radio stations on ships, aircraft, and railway locomotives (including multiple-unit trains, the same below) shall comply with the relevant provisions of the State, and the radio regulatory authority of the relevant department of the State Council shall issue radio station licenses; if a radio station identification code is required, the radio station identification code shall be issued concurrently. The relevant departments of the State Council shall regularly report the issuance of standard-type radio station licenses and radio station identification codes to the national radio regulatory authority.
The administrative measures for the establishment and use of non-standard-type radio stations on ships, aircraft and railway locomotives shall be formulated by the national radio regulatory authority jointly with the relevant departments of the State Council.

Article 37 In the event of an emergency that endangers national security, public safety, or safety of life and property, or for the special needs of ensuring major social activities, a radio station (or station) may be temporarily established and used without approval, but the matter shall be promptly reported to the radio regulatory authority at the location of the radio station (or station), and the station shall be promptly shut down after the emergency is eliminated or the major social activity ends.

Article 38 A radio station (or station) shall be established and used in accordance with the licensed matters and conditions specified in the radio station license; if the licensed matters are modified, the modification formalities shall be completed with the radio regulatory authority that made the licensing decision.
Where a radio station (or station) ceases to be used, the user shall promptly complete the cancellation formalities with the radio regulatory authority that made the licensing decision, return the radio station license, and dismantle the radio station (or station) and its antennas and other ancillary equipment.

Article 39 The unit or individual using a radio station (or station) shall conduct regular maintenance on the radio station (or station) to ensure that its performance indicators comply with national standards and the relevant provisions on national radio management, and to avoid causing harmful interference to other radio stations (or stations) legally established and used.

Article 40 The unit or individual using a radio station (or station) shall comply with the provisions on environmental protection of the State, and take necessary measures to prevent environmental pollution caused by electromagnetic radiation from radio wave emission.

A unit or individual using a radio station shall not intentionally transmit or receive radio signals beyond the scope permitted by the radio station license, and shall not disseminate, publish, or utilize unintentionally received information.
Amateur radio stations may only be used for mutual communication, technical research, and self-training, and shall transmit and receive signals within the frequency ranges dedicated to amateur services or amateur-satellite services, except for participation in emergency response to major natural disasters and other emergencies.
The radio frequencies used for developing radio transmission equipment shall comply with the national radio frequency allocation regulations.

The production or import of radio transmission equipment for sale or use within China shall comply with laws and regulations on product quality, national standards, and relevant provisions on national radio administration.

Except for micro-power short-range radio transmission equipment, the production or import of other radio transmission equipment for sale or use within China shall apply to the national radio administration institution for type approval. The catalogue of radio transmission equipment subject to type approval shall be published by the national radio administration institution.
The production or import of radio transmission equipment required to obtain type approval shall, in addition to complying with Article 43 of these Regulations, also comply with the technical specifications verified in the radio transmission equipment type approval certificate, and shall affix the type approval code on the equipment.

The national radio administration institution shall, according to law, review whether the radio transmission equipment applying for type approval meets the conditions specified in Article 45 of these Regulations, and shall make a decision to approve or disapprove within 30 working days from the date of accepting the application. If approved, it shall issue a radio transmission equipment type approval certificate; if disapproved, it shall notify the applicant in writing and state the reasons.
The national radio administration institution shall regularly publish the status of type approval of radio transmission equipment to the public.

For the import of radio transmission equipment that shall obtain type approval in accordance with Article 44 of these Regulations, the consignee of imported goods, the person carrying radio transmission equipment into the country, and the recipient of radio transmission equipment sent by mail shall voluntarily declare to the customs and go through customs clearance procedures by presenting the radio transmission equipment type approval certificate.
For activities such as sports competitions and scientific experiments, if it is necessary to carry or send by mail radio transmission equipment that shall obtain type approval in accordance with Article 44 of these Regulations but has not obtained it, for temporary entry, it shall be approved by the radio administration institution, and customs clearance procedures shall be handled with the approval document.

For the sale of radio transmission equipment that shall obtain type approval in accordance with Article 44 of these Regulations, the seller shall register the sale with the radio administration institution of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government. Radio transmission equipment without the type approval code affixed in accordance with these Regulations shall not be sold.
When repairing radio transmission equipment, the technical specifications verified in the radio transmission equipment type approval certificate shall not be altered.

The development, production, sale, and maintenance of high-power radio transmission equipment shall take measures to effectively suppress radio wave emission, and shall not cause harmful interference to radio stations legally established and used. For conducting actual emission tests, the procedures for temporary establishment and use of a radio station shall be applied to the radio administration institution of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government in accordance with Article 30 of these Regulations.

Foreign-related matters of radio frequency coordination and mutual harmful interference between stations within China and stations outside China shall be handled through coordination by the national radio administration institution together with relevant units and the relevant international organizations or countries/regions.
If it is necessary to provide radio administration-related materials to the International Telecommunication Union or other countries/regions, the national radio administration institution shall handle it uniformly.
The establishment and use of radio stations in border areas shall comply with the radio frequency coordination agreements signed between China and the relevant countries/regions.

If foreign leaders visiting China, foreign embassies and consulates in China, and representative offices of international organizations enjoying diplomatic privileges and immunities in China need to establish and use radio stations, they shall be approved by the national radio administration institution through diplomatic channels.
Except for transportation in diplomatic bags, if foreign leaders visiting China, foreign embassies and consulates in China, and representative offices of international organizations enjoying diplomatic privileges and immunities in China carry, send by mail, or otherwise transport radio transmission equipment that shall obtain type approval in accordance with Article 44 of these Regulations but has not obtained it, into the country, they shall obtain approval from the national radio administration institution through diplomatic channels and then go through customs clearance procedures.
If other overseas organizations or individuals establish and use radio stations within China, they shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions of China, obtain approval from the radio administration institution through the competent department of the relevant business; if they carry, send by mail, or otherwise transport radio transmission equipment that shall obtain type approval in accordance with Article 44 of these Regulations but has not obtained it, into the country, they shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions of China, obtain approval from the radio administration institution through the competent department of the relevant business and then go through the entry procedures for radio transmission equipment at the customs, unless the national radio administration institution specifies that approval is not required.

Radio stations installed on foreign vessels (including offshore platforms), aircraft, railway locomotives, vehicles, etc., when used within China, shall comply with China's laws and regulations and international treaties concluded or acceded to by China.

Overseas organizations or individuals shall not conduct radio wave parameter testing or radio wave monitoring within China.
No unit or individual shall provide domestic radio wave parameter data involving national security to overseas organizations or individuals.

The radio administration institution shall regularly inspect and test the use of radio frequencies and the radio stations in use, to ensure the normal use of radio stations and maintain normal radio wave order.

The National Radio Monitoring Center and the radio monitoring stations of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, as technical institutions for radio administration, shall, under the leadership of the national radio administration institution and the radio administration institutions of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government respectively, monitor radio signals, and search for radio interference sources and unauthorized radio stations.
The radio monitoring stations of the relevant departments of the State Council shall be responsible for monitoring radio signals within their respective systems (industries).

The radio wave radiation generated by industrial, scientific, and medical equipment, electrified transportation systems, high-voltage power lines, and other electrical devices shall comply with national standards and relevant provisions on national radio administration.
When formulating national standards and technical specifications for non-radio equipment that radiates radio waves, the opinions of the national radio administration institution shall be solicited.

If non-radio equipment that radiates radio waves causes harmful interference to radio stations that have been legally established and used, the owner or user of the equipment shall take measures to eliminate it.

Article 61 The siting and location of engineering facilities that generate radio wave radiation and are determined by the radio regulatory authority, which may cause harmful interference to radio stations (stations) that have been set up and used according to law, shall be determined through consultation between the competent department of urban and rural planning of the local people's government and the radio regulatory authority of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government.

Article 62 For the construction of projects such as radio astronomy observatories, meteorological radar stations, satellite tracking, telemetry and command (navigation) stations, and airports that require special protection of the electromagnetic environment, the project construction entity shall, before determining the project site, conduct electromagnetic compatibility analysis and demonstration on the site and solicit opinions from the radio regulatory authority; if no electromagnetic compatibility analysis and demonstration is conducted, or the opinions of the radio regulatory authority are not solicited or adopted, it shall not raise a request to the radio regulatory authority for the elimination of harmful interference.

Article 63 In the surrounding areas of existing radio astronomy observatories, meteorological radar stations, satellite tracking, telemetry and command (navigation) stations, and airports, no tall buildings or facilities that block the transmission of radio signals shall be newly constructed, and no facilities or equipment that interfere with their normal use shall be set up or used. The radio regulatory authority shall, jointly with the competent department of urban and rural planning and other relevant departments, formulate specific protection measures and make them public.

Article 64 The State shall provide special protection for radio frequencies relating to personal safety, such as radio navigation, distress and rescue, and safety communication exclusively used by ships, spacecraft, aircraft, and railway locomotives. If any radio transmitting equipment or non-radio equipment that radiates radio waves causes harmful interference to such frequencies, the harmful interference shall be eliminated immediately.

Article 65 If a radio station (station) set up and used according to law suffers harmful interference, it may file a complaint with the radio regulatory authority. The radio regulatory authority that accepts the complaint shall handle it in a timely manner and inform the complainant of the handling situation.
The handling of mutual harmful interference between radio frequencies shall follow the principles that out-of-band gives way to in-band, secondary services give way to primary services, later use gives way to earlier use, and unplanned use gives way to planned use.

Article 66 The radio regulatory authority may require a radio station (station) that generates harmful interference to take measures such as repairing the radio transmitting equipment, calibrating the transmission frequency, or reducing power to eliminate the harmful interference; if the harmful interference cannot be eliminated, it may order the radio station (station) that generates the harmful interference to suspend transmission.

Article 67 For illegal radio transmission activities, the radio regulatory authority may impound the radio transmitting equipment or seal up the radio station (station), and when necessary may take technical blocking measures; if the radio regulatory authority discovers suspected illegal or criminal activities during radio monitoring and inspection, it shall promptly notify the public security organ and cooperate with the investigation and handling.

Article 68 The radio regulatory authority of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government shall strengthen supervision and inspection over the production and sale of radio transmitting equipment, and investigate and deal with illegal acts according to law. The product quality supervision department and the administrative department for industry and commerce of the local people's government at or above the county level shall cooperate with the supervision and inspection, and promptly report to the radio regulatory authority any illegal production or sale of radio transmitting equipment discovered in the course of product quality supervision or market supervision enforcement.

Article 69 The staff members of the radio regulatory authority and the radio monitoring center (station) shall keep confidential the communication secrets and radio signals learned of in the course of performing their duties.

Article 70 Anyone who, in violation of these Regulations, uses a radio frequency without a license, or sets up or uses a radio station (station) without authorization, shall be ordered by the radio regulatory authority to make corrections, and his equipment used for the illegal activities and illegal gains shall be confiscated, and a fine of not more than 50,000 yuan may also be imposed; if he refuses to make corrections, a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan shall also be imposed; if he sets up or uses a radio station (station) without authorization to engage in fraudulent or other illegal activities, which does not yet constitute a crime, a fine of not less than 200,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan shall also be imposed.

Article 71 Anyone who, in violation of these Regulations, transfers a radio frequency without authorization shall be ordered by the radio regulatory authority to make corrections, and his illegal gains shall be confiscated; if he refuses to make corrections, a fine of not less than one time but not more than three times the illegal gains shall also be imposed; if there are no illegal gains or the illegal gains are less than 100,000 yuan, a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan shall be imposed; if serious consequences are caused, his radio frequency use permit shall be revoked.

Article 73 Anyone who, in violation of these Regulations, uses radio transmitting equipment or non-radio equipment that radiates radio waves to interfere with the normal conduct of radio services shall be ordered by the radio regulatory authority to make corrections; if he refuses to make corrections, the equipment that generates harmful interference shall be confiscated, and a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan shall be imposed, and his radio station license shall be revoked; if harmful interference is caused to radio frequencies exclusively used by ships, spacecraft, aircraft, and railway locomotives for radio navigation, distress and rescue, and safety communication, which involve personal safety, a fine of not less than 200,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan shall also be imposed.

Article 74 Anyone who fails to pay the radio frequency occupancy fee in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State shall be ordered by the radio regulatory authority to pay within a specified time limit; if he fails to pay within the time limit, a late payment fee of 0.05% per day shall be imposed from the date of default.

Article 76 Anyone who, in violation of these Regulations, produces or imports radio transmitting equipment that is sold or used within China without obtaining type approval shall be ordered by the radio regulatory authority to make corrections, and a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan shall be imposed; if he refuses to make corrections, the radio transmitting equipment without type approval shall be confiscated, and a fine of not less than 200,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan shall also be imposed.

Article 77 Anyone who sells radio transmitting equipment that, in accordance with Article 44 of these Regulations, is required to obtain type approval but fails to go through the sales recordation formalities with the radio regulatory authority shall be ordered by the radio regulatory authority to make corrections; if he refuses to make corrections, a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 30,000 yuan shall be imposed.

Article 78 Anyone who sells radio transmitting equipment that, in accordance with Article 44 of these Regulations, is required to obtain type approval but has not obtained type approval shall be ordered by the radio regulatory authority to make corrections, and the illegally sold radio transmitting equipment and illegal gains shall be confiscated, and a fine of not more than 10% of the value of the illegally sold equipment may also be imposed; if he refuses to make corrections, a fine of not less than 10% but not more than 30% of the value of the illegally sold equipment shall also be imposed.

Article 79 Anyone who, in the course of repairing radio transmitting equipment, alters the technical specifications verified in the radio transmitting equipment type approval certificate shall be ordered by the radio regulatory authority to make corrections; if he refuses to make corrections, a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 30,000 yuan shall be imposed.

Article 80 If the production or sale of radio transmitting equipment violates laws and regulations on product quality management, the product quality supervision department shall impose penalties according to law.
If the import of radio transmitting equipment, or carrying, sending by post, or transporting radio transmitting equipment into the country by other means violates laws and regulations on customs supervision, the customs shall impose penalties according to law.

Article 81 Anyone who, in violation of these Regulations, commits an act violating public security administration shall be given a public security penalty according to law; if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 82 Where the radio regulatory agency and its staff fail to perform their duties in accordance with the provisions of these Regulations, the responsible leaders and other directly responsible persons shall be given disciplinary sanctions according to law.

Article 83 Where a license under these Regulations requires completion of relevant domestic or international coordination or fulfillment of procedures specified by international rules, the time for carrying out such coordination and procedures shall not be counted within the time limit for license review.

Article 84 The radio management of military systems shall be implemented in accordance with the relevant military provisions.
For radio management involving radio and television broadcasting, if there are separate provisions by other laws and administrative regulations, those provisions shall prevail.
Article 85 These Regulations shall come into force as of December 1, 2016.
